chapter_title: The Chapter of the Commandments of Righteousness
chapter_note: This chapter contains no oldest teaching substrate. It is entirely institutional material prescribing community rules for the Manichaean elect (three seals: continence, rest of hands, purity of mouth) and catechumens (fasting, prayer, almsgiving; giving persons to the church; building for the church). Teaching purity is near zero (0.033). The only cosmological term ('Cross of Light' in ¶1) is used as a reference point for a behavioral commandment, not as part of a cosmic-correspondential mapping. The chapter's voice is consistently prescriptive — it tells people what to DO, never describes what cosmic structures ARE. The massive institutional vocabulary drift (5.78→30.12) confirms the chapter is a single institutional composition, not substrate with editorial overlay.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with dialogue frame formula 'Once more the enlightener speaks to his disciples' followed by prescriptive rules for the elect: the three seals (continence, rest of hands, purity of mouth). The 'Cross of Light' is a cosmological term but functions here as a reference point for a behavioral commandment ('keep his hand still before the Cross of Light' = don't harm vegetation), not as cosmological mapping. The voice is entirely prescriptive: 'a person will do', 'he can embrace', 'he will keep'. No domain-to-domain cosmic mapping present.

The 'second righteousness' for the elect: multiply wisdom, faith, and grace among others. Entirely prescriptive and community-oriented: 'from his wisdom he can give wisdom, to every person who will hear it from him.' This describes community duties of the elect — evangelism, sharing faith — not cosmic structure. The vocabulary is pastoral/institutional ('give wisdom', 'give faith', 'give freely of love', 'cause others to be sent').

Transition paragraph bridging from elect rules to catechumen rules. Pure institutional vocabulary: 'perfect elect', 'catechumen', 'catechumen of the faith', 'perfected in two stages.' This is organizational scaffolding for the Manichaean community structure.

Seam flag fires correctly — this is high-density institutional material. 'Fasting, prayer, and almsgiving' are the catechumenate's first work. Specific institutional practices: fasting on the lord's day, praying to sun and moon, giving alms to the holy ones. 'Lord's day' and 'catechumenate' are strong institutional markers. The prayer to sun and moon could reflect older cosmological veneration but here serves as a prescribed practice.

Second work of the catechumenate: giving persons to the church (children, relatives, rescued persons, purchased slaves). Entirely about community organization and support for the ecclesiastical structure. No cosmological content whatsoever.
Third work: building dwellings or places for 'a portion of alms in the holy church.' Pure institutional material about physical support for the community. Very high institutional density (32.0).

Summary paragraph recapping the three catechumen works. Seam flag fires — highest institutional density in the chapter (35.21). Promises rewards for catechumens who fulfill obligations: 'great love therein, and a share of every grace and good in the holy church.' This is institutional encouragement/exhortation directed at the catechumen community. The editorial fatigue pattern is evident — institutional vocabulary peaks in this final paragraph.
